title: HA/DR automation: multi-AZ Terraform + Helm updates + runbooks-as-code + restore-drill tooling
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in regulated environments requested an automated, codified HA/DR workflow for multi-AZ deployments and restore drills. This PR bundles Terraform module updates (multi-AZ networking and instance placement), Helm chart changes (readiness/leader-elections, probe tuning, podDisruptionBudget), an upgrade/rollback helper in the installer, and runbooks-as-code for restore drills and failover playbooks. The goal is to make day-2 operations reproducible: create multi-AZ clusters, initiate controlled failovers, validate data plane recovery, and exercise upgrade rollback paths.

This PR includes: - Terraform: new module inputs for availability_zone_count, cross_az_subnets, and improved state locking guidance; automated testvars for simulation of AZ failures. - Helm: leader-election sidecar optional flag, tuned liveness/readiness thresholds for high-latency inter-AZ traffic, additional annotations for PodDisruptionBudget and topologySpreadConstraints. - Installer tooling: upgrade_and_rollback.sh to perform canary upgrade, automatic snapshot before upgrade, rollback helper that re-applies last-known-good release and database restore steps. - Runbooks-as-code: ha-dr/runbooks/* as machine-readable runbooks (YAML -> rendered markdown) plus a restore-drill runner that executes validation checks and posts results to Slack channel and incident API. - Tests: end-to-end restore drill harness that runs in CI using small fixture clusters (simulated AZ drain) and smoke tests to assert service routing and KV cache warmup.

Checklist: - [x] Terraform modules updated and backward compatible defaults provided - [x] Helm chart bump + migration notes - [x] Installer upgrade/rollback helper + tests - [x] Runbooks-as-code added and documentation generated - [x] CI jobs added for restore-drill smoke test - [x] Security review for S3 snapshot handling and KMS integration

Impact and rollback: Changes are additive and guarded by feature flags. The installer helper is opt-in and requires RBAC permissions documented in the runbook. If issues are detected on a canary, the helper will automatically trigger the rollback flow which was verified by the restore-drill CI.

Related: ENG-4123 for automation scope, OPS-1190 for incident-driven requirements, SUP-333 customer case that requested multi-AZ failover automation.
